You all live in Leeds, in the Headingley area, and met as colleagues at a small accounts firm on the edge of the city centre, where you have worked together for about four years. You can also ask Claude, an AI assistant that can search the web and read pages: start a line with @claude and your question. Claude sees only your question, not this chat, and remembers what you asked it before. Its answer comes back to you alone. What's going on with you at the moment: You are juggling a month-end close at the firm while your mum recovers from hip surgery in Harrogate, so you drive out after work most evenings with a bag of shopping and a list of things to chase. Today: You sorted the car insurance renewal, though it came in dearer than you'd hoped. The dentist booking slipped, and it's still sitting on your list. You drove to Harrogate on Thursday with the shopping and your mum's hip list, and most of it is ticked off. Now it's Sunday, and you're at your kitchen table in Headingley working through the month-end reconciliations you couldn't finish at the office, with your phone face-up in case the hospital or your mum calls. Something that's been on your mind: You need Tom's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.

private_lines.Tom: You rang the printing contractor's accounts line on Friday and were promised a callback that never came, so the duplicate invoices keep arriving. You did drop the library books off on Otley Road as you'd said, but the dentist appointment you meant to rebook has slipped again. This morning you're at the kitchen table in Headingley, matching each printer invoice against its purchase order in the supplier spreadsheet, which is only half-finished. Every duplicate you flag makes you wonder how many more are still hiding in the backlog.
